text:
alex: FYI — AcmePay (tenant-acmepay) is getting a wave of 429s + P99 spikes on Dedicated pool-3 since 2025-03-01T14:10:00Z. Looks correlated with kv cache eviction spikes. attaching quick logs and a metric snapshot.

maria: thanks alex — can you paste tenant id, sample request_id(s), and the exact time window you saw spikes?

alex: tenant-acmepay; sample req ids: r_9f7a2c, r_9f7a9; window 14:08–14:18 UTC. metric highlights: 
```
kv_evictions/sec: 0.4 -> 180 (14:11)
kv_cache_hits: down 92% -> 47%
p99_latency_ms: 85 -> 1120
auth_429s: 0 -> 120/min
autoscaler_events: scale_up 4->8 @14:12, cool_down 300s
```

junaid: I pulled infra logs — saw repeated slab_compact and kv_reclaim logs around 14:11. sounds like memory fragmentation + long-context ridge. Any recent changes to session length or model config?

alex: customer says they started a campaign that drives long-session chat (many >40k token prefixes). No model change on our side — tenant pinned to redwood/gpt-mini-2025-v1.

tess: long-context + many concurrent sessions will blow up KV usage. posible causes: prefix cache growth + eviction thrashing + slab fragmentation. quick mitigation: reduce per-session kv_window or enable per-tenant kv_reserve. Command to change tenant policy: 
```
# temporary: reserve 8GB KV for tenant-acmepay
redwoodctl tenant update tenant-acmepay --kv-reserve 8G
```

alex: repro steps I used on staging (shared so you can run):
1) create 100 concurrent websocket sessions to /v1/chat with conversation history ~55k tokens
2) send a 2-token user message every 8s for 10 minutes
3) observe kv_evictions/sec and p99 latency via /metrics

curl example to start session: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.company/v1/sessions -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"tenant":"tenant-acmepay","model":"gpt-mini-2025-v1","mode":"stream-longseq"}'
```

deploy-bot: autoscaler: scaled pool-3 from 4 -> 8 @ 2025-03-01T14:12:08Z, backlog peaked at 520 requests, cooldown until 14:17:08Z. No failed pods reported.

ryan: can we confirm memory fragmentation metrics? look for kv_frag_ratio and slab_reclaims. If kv_frag_ratio > 0.6 we should consider slab compaction tuning. Query we use: 
```
promql: sum(rate(kv_evictions_total[1m])) by (tenant)
promql: max(kv_frag_ratio) by (pool)
```

elaine: opened INC-2025-ACME-KV with support and created a side channel with the customer. asked them to enable short-term per-session limits while we investigate.

maria: temporary config we applied for AcmePay in prod: 
```
redwoodctl tenant update tenant-acmepay --kv-policy soft-limit --kv-soft-limit 0.8
```
this should reduce immediate evictions but keep service up. please confirm if 429s drop. :thumbsup:

kevin: noted increased token usage in billing — moving to review after incident. FYI finance will flag large spikes for ACME.

alex: plan proposal:
- junaid reproduce on staging and capture heap + slab traces (owner: junaid)
- tess implement eviction backoff + prefer-LRU patch to reduce snowballing evictions (owner: tess)
- ryan validate slab compaction thresholds and consider lowering compaction aggression on Dedicated pools
- support apply per-tenant kv_reserve/soft-limits as mitigation and notify customer

who wants to pick the immediate patch? we should aim for a canary tomorrow.

tess: I'll take the eviction backoff patch. aiming for PR + canary by EOD tomorrow. patch idea: add an exponentially increasing backoff for entries evicted due to long-prefix churn and prefer freeing small prefix segments first.

junaid: I'll run the staging load (using alex's steps) and attach flamegraphs + prom snapshots. will validate that kv_reserve stops the 429s. :eyes:

maria: once junaid confirms mitigation works, I'll coordinate a maintenance window with AcmePay to roll the soft-limit and then the canary patch.

alex: thanks all — please drop results in this thread. tagging @tess @junaid @ryan @elaine to keep aligned. :pray:
